title.narrative: Enhanced capacity of constituents to anticipate skills needs and to develop and implement inclusive skills policies and programmes for youth, vulnerable groups and forcibly displaced people

description.narrative: The Education and Training Policy (2023) of Ethiopia identified some of the critical challenges that affect skills development in the country that the quality of the TVET system does not respond to labour market demands due to: (i) lack of adequate quality assurance system, (ii) inadequate and outdated equipment, (iii) TVET trainer’s lack of industry experience, and (iv) poor training infrastructure. Through this CPO, the ILO will support constituents on skills needs anticipation in key economic sectors, with a view to increasing value added and skills levels. Assistance will be provided on assessing the overall skills system and prepare recommendations on a medium to long-term plan to strengthen TVET and increase skills levels, with focus to inclusion of marginalized populations such as, refugees, migrants PWDs, women and rural youth. In addition, the ILO supports the country’s TVET system in providing technical support to implement the new education and training policy 2023, on reviewing and updating of occupational standards, core skills, skills for a greener future, recognition of prior learning (RPL), implementing capacity building for the ministry of labour and skills and others mentioned in training policy. Support will also be extended to the Ministry of Labour and Skills to develop a National Work Ethics and Culture Strategy. The Strategy will serve to enhance soft skills, produce a competitive workforce, and improve the performance of organizations. ILO will partner with the Ministry of Women and Social Affairs to revise the National Youth Policy. The revision will allow Ethiopia to incorporate the traditionally underrepresented forcibly displaced people be part of the consultation and policy revision, and its implementation. The interventions to achieve the CPO will be channelled through the programmes such as PROSPECTS, BRMM, Pro Agro as well as the Global Programme on Skills and Lifelong Learning (GPSL3) – Ethiopia component.
